message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – originally for rasterizing images, now also used for massively parallel compute tasks. |
| **Architecture** | Few cores (typically 2–32) with complex control logic, large caches, high clock speeds, and sophisticated branch prediction. | Hundreds or thousands of simpler cores optimized for throughput; each core is smaller and less capable of handling complex branching. |
| **Instruction set** | Rich, complex instruction sets (x86, ARM) with support for many data types and advanced features. | Often a subset of the CPU’s ISA or a specialized SIMD instruction set; focuses on vector operations. |
| **Execution model** | Serial or lightly parallel – one thread per core, with hyper‑threading to hide latency. | Highly parallel – thousands of threads run simultaneously on many cores. |
| **Memory hierarchy** | Large L1/L2/L3 caches, sophisticated memory controllers, low latency access to main memory. | Smaller per‑core caches, relies on high bandwidth memory (HBM, GDDR) and shared memory pools. |
| **Typical workloads** | Single‑threaded or lightly threaded tasks: OS kernel, database queries, web servers, office apps. | Data‑parallel tasks: image/video processing, scientific simulations, machine learning inference/training, cryptocurrency mining. |
| **Power consumption** | Lower power per core, but overall power can be high when many cores are active. | High raw throughput per watt; GPUs are efficient at doing the same operation on many data elements. |

In short, CPUs excel at tasks that require complex decision making and low latency, while GPUs shine when you need to perform the same operation on a huge number of data items in parallel. That’s why modern systems often combine both: the CPU handles general control flow, and the GPU accelerates heavy‑lifting compute or graphics rendering.
